skill.name: exa-cli
skill.description: Run Exa web search and code-context lookups from a local Python CLI. Use it to retrieve current web sources, programming references, and library usage context.
skill.summary: Search current web and programming context through the Exa MCP service.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Python CLI that sends search and code-context requests to the Exa MCP endpoint. Most Markdown backtick and entropy alerts are false positives, but network access, token handling, and direct script execution are real. No prompt injection or intentionally malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Environment tokens can be sent to a custom endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Only send EXA_API_KEY or EXA_MCP_TOKEN to the default Exa endpoint, or require explicit confirmation for other endpoints.

remediation.issue: The CLI supports passing tokens as command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or a secure credential store, and warn users that command arguments can be logged locally.

remediation.issue: The skill requires executing a bundled Python script.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external network destination, dependency requirements, and expected local cache writes before execution.

content.user_title: Search Web and Code Context with Exa
content.value_statement: Current technical answers often require live web sources and focused code references. This skill runs Exa searches from the CLI and returns web or programming context for review.
actual_capabilities: Runs Exa web searches through the web-search-exa command.
Uses an Exa MCP endpoint with optional bearer token authentication.
Supports result count, crawl mode, context length, timeout, and cache controls.
Can print formatted results or full structured output for inspection.
Caches MCP initialization and tool-list responses for faster repeated calls.
limitations: Requires network access to the configured Exa MCP endpoint.
Requires an Exa API key or MCP token for authenticated usage.
Search quality and availability depend on the Exa service.
A custom endpoint can receive queries and authorization headers.

use_cases.title: Verify Current API Guidance
use_cases.description: Search recent official sources before changing code that depends on external APIs.

use_cases.title: Collect Technical Research Sources
use_cases.description: Find relevant web pages and context snippets for a technical decision or comparison.

use_cases.title: Find Programming Context
use_cases.description: Retrieve focused context about libraries, errors, or framework behavior before drafting documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Web Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a simple current-information lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use exa-cli to search for current official guidance about {topic}. Summarize the strongest sources with links.

prompt_templates.title: Library Usage Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Find programming references for a library or framework task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use get-code-context-exa for {library} {task}. Return the relevant guidance, source names, and any version details.

prompt_templates.title: Source Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare multiple current sources before making a recommendation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use web-search-exa to compare recent sources about {decision}. Identify agreements, conflicts, and the most authoritative links.

prompt_templates.title: Tuned Research Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Use advanced options for deeper research with bounded output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use exa-cli with an appropriate result count and context limit for {research question}. Prefer authoritative sources and note uncertainty.

output_examples.input: Search for current Exa MCP authentication guidance.
output_examples.output: A concise list of relevant sources with links, dates when available, and notes about required token handling.

output_examples.input: Find code context for a Python httpx timeout issue.
output_examples.output: A focused explanation of likely timeout settings, related library behavior, and source references to inspect next.

output_examples.input: Compare recent guidance for a framework migration.
output_examples.output: A short comparison of official documentation, release notes, and credible examples, with conflicts called out clearly.

best_practices: Prefer official documentation and primary sources when reviewing search results.
Use environment variables for tokens instead of command-line token arguments.
Set result and context limits to keep outputs focused and reviewable.
anti_patterns: Do not send private code, secrets, or customer data as search queries.
Do not use an untrusted custom endpoint with environment-based tokens enabled.
Do not treat search output as authoritative without checking source quality.

faq.question: What does this skill connect to?
faq.answer: It connects to the configured Exa MCP endpoint, which defaults to the hosted Exa MCP service.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Authenticated use requires a token from EXA_API_KEY, EXA_MCP_TOKEN, or the --token option.

faq.question: Can it search for code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The get-code-context-exa command is intended for programming questions and library usage context.

faq.question: Can I change the endpoint?
faq.answer: Yes, but only use trusted endpoints because authorization headers and queries are sent there.

faq.question: Does it cache results?
faq.answer: It caches MCP initialization and tool-list responses, not full search result content.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
